therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: lipid-lowering via PPAR-alpha activation (fenofibrate) and niacin receptor agonism
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: dyslipidemia correction and cardiovascular risk reduction
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: HIV-infected individuals with lipodystrophy or dyslipidemia
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Triglycerides, Non-HDL-C, HDL-C, Total Cholesterol, Total Cholesterol:HDL-C Ratio at 24 weeks

results.effect_size: Triglycerides: 135.6 mg/dL (combo) vs 199 mg/dL (usual care); HDL-C: 44.8 mg/dL (combo) vs 37.1 mg/dL (usual care); TC:HDL ratio: 4.0 (combo) vs 5.2 (usual care)
biomarker_changes: Adiponectin highest in Diet/Exercise+Niacin arm (11.01 mcg/mL) vs usual care (7.12 mcg/mL)
HOMA-IR highest in Diet/Exercise+Niacin arm (2.76) vs usual care (1.92)
Insulin sensitivity index lowest in combo arms (2.38) vs usual care (3.54)
Body cell mass highest in combo arm (68.2 kg) vs usual care (59.6 kg)
Fat mass similar across arms (35.8–37.7 kg)
subgroup_findings: Niacin arms showed higher adiponectin but also higher HOMA-IR suggesting possible insulin resistance worsening
Diet/Exercise alone improved insulin sensitivity index (4.95) vs usual care (3.54)
Fenofibrate+Niacin combo achieved lowest triglycerides (135.6 mg/dL) and best TC:HDL ratio (4.0)
safety_signals: Elevated transaminases >3x ULN observed across arms including combo
Chest pain/angina reported in usual care, diet/exercise, fenofibrate, and niacin arms
Serum creatinine >1.5 mg/dL in usual care, fenofibrate, niacin, and combo arms
Triglycerides >1000 mg/dL in usual care (1/30), diet/exercise (3/38), and niacin (1/40) arms
Elevated bilirubin most common in usual care (3/30) and diet/exercise (5/38) arms

dose_info.dose: Niacin: up to 2 grams/day; Fenofibrate: 120 mg/day
dose_info.schedule: Niacin titrated up to 2 g/day; Fenofibrate 120 mg/day

adverse_events.term: Transaminases elevated >3 times upper normal limit

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Fenofibrate's PPAR-alpha-mediated triglyceride lowering complements niacin's HDL-raising and VLDL-suppressing effects, producing additive dyslipidemia correction beyond either agent alone
modulation_entries.citation: Diet/Exercise + Fenofibrate + Niacin arm achieved lowest triglycerides (135.6 mg/dL) and best TC:HDL ratio (4.0) compared to either drug alone

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Dietary modification reduces substrate availability for hepatic lipid synthesis, amplifying fenofibrate's PPAR-alpha-mediated triglyceride lowering
modulation_entries.citation: Diet/Exercise + Fenofibrate arm achieved triglycerides of 155.1 mg/dL vs 199 mg/dL in usual care

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Dietary modification reduces lipid substrate load, amplifying niacin's ability to raise HDL and lower triglycerides
modulation_entries.citation: Diet/Exercise + Niacin arm achieved triglycerides of 177.6 mg/dL and HDL-C of 41.8 mg/dL vs 199 mg/dL and 37.1 mg/dL in usual care
